text:
Priya R.: hey folks, hitting a weird routing problem on my home network — can't pull images from our internal registry (10.42.12.4) while on the split-tunnel VPN. Office wifi works fine. MacBook Pro M2, macOS Monterey, using the official WireGuard client. ssh to rdw-bastion.company.internal just times out. anyone seen CG-NAT + split-tunnel cause this?

Ben (DevOps): are you on WireGuard or OpenVPN? can you paste the output of `ip route get 10.42.12.4` and `scutil --dns` + a `traceroute 10.42.12.4`? also which utun/tun interface shows up for the VPN?

Priya R.: pasted outputs below — sorry for the long one, i copied straight from terminal:
```
$ ip route get 10.42.12.4
10.42.12.4 via 100.64.0.1 dev en0 src 192.168.1.12
    cache
$ traceroute 10.42.12.4
traceroute to 10.42.12.4 (10.42.12.4), 64 hops max, 52 byte packets
 1  192.168.1.1 (192.168.1.1)  1.123 ms  0.987 ms  1.045 ms
 2  * * *
 3  * * *
```
scutil output looks like normal resolver entries for our corp DNS but i can resolve hostnames when office VPN is on. here it just times out.

Ben (DevOps): yeah that `via 100.64.x.x` is a sign your ISP is using CG‑NAT (100.64.0.0/10). hairpinning to RFC1918 addresses across split-tunnel can fail when the path goes through the ISP NAT. two pragmatic workarounds: 1) add an explicit route for the internal subnets via the VPN interface (utunX) so packets don't try to go out your default CG‑NAT path, or 2) use the bastion SOCKS proxy to tunnel docker/pip requests through SSH.

For 1) find the interface name (run `ifconfig` and look for utun* created by WireGuard) then:`sudo route -n add -net 10.42.0.0/16 -interface utun2` (replace utun2 with yours). That forces internal traffic over the VPN.

For 2) quick socks approach: `ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_rdw -D 1080 rdw-bastion` then set `HTTP_PROXY=socks5://localhost:1080` and `HTTPS_PROXY=socks5://localhost:1080` for your build/pull commands. Works well for ad-hoc pulls without switching to full-tunnel.

Carla: we also have per-user bastion hostnames (e.g., `rdw-bastion-priya`) which are allowed to accept internal-forwarding from the public side — if you prefer an ssh ProxyJump pattern you can add this to `~/.ssh/config`:
```
Host rdw-bastion-priya
  HostName rdw-bastion.company.internal
  User priya
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_rdw
\nHost rdw-registry
  HostName internal-registry.company.internal
  ProxyJump rdw-bastion-priya
```
That lets `ssh rdw-registry` or `scp` go through the bastion without fiddling with SOCKS. I'll check your account has the per-user bounce configured.

Priya R.: tried the SOCKS trick: `ssh -D 1080 -i ~/.ssh/id_rdw rdw-bastion` then `export DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1` and `export HTTP_PROXY=socks5://localhost:1080` before `docker build`. The base image pull succeeded. so this unblocks my onboarding scripts for now. thanks! :relieved:

Ben (DevOps): great. i'll open a small infra ticket to add an onboarding note and an automated check that detects CG‑NAT on macOS and suggests the explicit route or full-tunnel option. tagging @Carla to follow up on per-user bastion bounce config.

Infra Bot: Created ticket INF-621: "Onboarding: doc + detection for CG-NAT / split-tunnel issues" assigned to DevOps.

Carla: noted, i've linked INF-621 to the new-hires checklist and i'll add the ssh config snippet to the private onboarding doc.

Priya R.: awesome — leaving this thread in case others hit the same thing. thanks again everyone :thumbsup:
